cards.title: Bayesian Active Object Recognition and 6D Pose Estimation from Multimodal Contact Sensing
cards.problem: Joint object class and 6D pose estimation via active tactile exploration with ambiguity from sparse contacts.
cards.method: Bayesian belief over class and pose using customized progressive particle filter; fuses wrist force/torque, GelSight contact and free-space (non-contact) constraints; belief guides selection of informative next touches under reachability constraints; motion planning with tactile servoing.
cards.data: Simulation and a Franka Panda robot using 11 YCB objects.
cards.metrics: Recognition and pose estimation accuracy and stability; number of action cycles.
cards.findings: Incorporating tactile and free-space information substantially improves recognition and pose accuracy and stability and reduces the number of action cycles versus force/torque-only baselines (no numeric values in abstract).
cards.limitations: Next-touch selection is belief-guided per step, apparently one-step (inferred); known object set of 11 YCB objects (inferred); online particle-filter inference with no amortized/learned policy; decision latency not stated in abstract; no information-bound training of a policy.
cards.citation: Haodong Zheng, Gabriele M. Caddeo, Andrei C. Jalba, et al.. Bayesian Active Object Recognition and 6D Pose Estimation from Multimodal Contact Sensing. arXiv (Cornell University), 2026. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2603.21410

cards.title: A Bayesian Framework for Active Tactile Object Recognition, Pose Estimation and Shape Transfer Learning
cards.problem: Active tactile object recognition, pose estimation and shape transfer learning including novel objects.
cards.method: Customized particle filter jointly updating class and pose while tracking novelty; GPIS reconstructs novel shapes with prior grounded in PF MAP estimate; exploration guided by global shape estimation with termination on sufficient information.
cards.metrics: Not stated in abstract (effectiveness and efficiency of class and pose estimation, novel-shape learning).
cards.findings: Framework is effective and efficient for class and pose of known objects, learns novel shapes and reliably recognizes previously learned shapes (qualitative).
cards.limitations: Simulation only (inferred); exploration rule based on global shape estimation, not a learned policy (inferred); no explicit non-myopic planning; no free-space evidence mentioned; latency not stated in abstract.
cards.citation: Haodong Zheng, Andrei C. Jalba, Raymond H. Cuijpers, et al.. A Bayesian Framework for Active Tactile Object Recognition, Pose Estimation and Shape Transfer Learning. arXiv (Cornell University), 2024. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2409.06912

cards.title: Active Tactile Exploration for Rigid Body Pose and Shape Estimation
cards.problem: Estimate shape and location of unseen rigid objects that may move on contact, using only tactile data with minimal robot motion.
cards.method: Contact-rich system-identification loss penalizing physical constraint violation without numerical stiffness; exploration scheme maximizing Expected Information Gain.
cards.data: Simulated and real-robot experiments (objects: cuboid and convex polyhedral geometries).
cards.metrics: Learning speed of shape and location (details not stated in abstract).
cards.findings: Can learn cuboid and convex polyhedral geometries with less than 10s of randomly collected data after first contact; EIG-maximizing exploration gives significantly faster learning in simulated and real-robot experiments.
cards.limitations: Geometry restricted to cuboids and convex polyhedra; EIG maximization appears per-step/myopic (inferred); optimization-based online learning, not an amortized policy (inferred); identity/class not addressed; latency not stated in abstract.
cards.citation: Ethan Kroll Gordon, Bruke Baraki, Hien Bui, et al.. Active Tactile Exploration for Rigid Body Pose and Shape Estimation. Proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation/Proceedings, 2026. doi:10.1109/icra57385.2026.11696035

cards.title: Efficient Touch Based Localization through Submodularity
cards.problem: Efficiently sequencing information-gathering touch actions for localization.
cards.method: Shows Shannon entropy reduction is submodular under certain assumptions so greedy is comparable to optimal offline; adaptive-submodularity-based online methods with guarantees versus optimal online policy and computational speedups.
cards.findings: Greedy selection (even with only one step lookahead) often performs well; entropy reduction is submodular under assumptions, giving guarantees for greedy versus optimal plan.
cards.limitations: Greedy / one-step selection by design with guarantees only under submodularity assumptions; no learned policy; no identity estimation stated; scalability and latency not stated in abstract.
cards.citation: Shervin Javdani, Matthew Klingensmith, James Andrew Bagnell, et al.. Efficient Touch Based Localization through Submodularity. arXiv (Cornell University), 2012. doi:10.1184/r1/6554705

cards.title: The next best touch for model-based localization
cards.problem: Choose the next touch action to accurately localize an object.
cards.method: Information gain metric on pose uncertainty picks next best touch; estimator updates pose; extended to simultaneously estimate model parameter or model class.
cards.data: Simulation and experiment on the DARPA ARM-S robot.
cards.metrics: Information gain (uncertainty of pose); quantitative results not stated in abstract.
cards.findings: Next-best-touch selection by information gain localizes objects accurately in simulation and real experiment; extends to joint localization and model parameter/class estimation (qualitative).
cards.limitations: Greedy next-best-touch selection (inferred); information gain computed online, decision latency not stated in abstract; no learned or amortized policy; no free-space evidence mentioned.
cards.citation: Paul D. N. Hebert, Thomas M. Howard, Nicolas Hudson, et al.. The next best touch for model-based localization. Proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation/Proceedings, 2013. doi:10.1109/icra.2013.6630562

cards.title: Global Localization of Objects via Touch
cards.problem: Global 6-DOF localization of objects via touch, computationally prohibitive for full Bayesian posterior.
cards.method: Scaling Series: Monte Carlo successive refinements with annealing; analytical measurement model for polygonal meshes.
cards.data: Five common solid objects, rigidly fixed; also 6-DOF localization and tracking of free-standing objects.
cards.findings: Scaling Series solves the full problem reliably in real time and drastically outperforms prior approaches (qualitative).
cards.limitations: Estimator only; touch selection not addressed in abstract; known mesh models; five objects; real-time claim without latency figure in abstract.
cards.citation: Anna Petrovskaya, Oussama Khatib. Global Localization of Objects via Touch. IEEE Transactions on Robotics, 2011. doi:10.1109/tro.2011.2138450

cards.title: Touch based POMDP manipulation via sequential submodular optimization
cards.problem: Touch-based localization via adaptive submodularity scales poorly with system dimensionality at motion level.
cards.method: Integrates an action hierarchy into adaptive submodularity framework, motivated by hierarchical POMDP planning, using sequential submodular optimization.
cards.data: Simulated robot and Willow Garage PR2.
cards.findings: Adaptive submodularity gives near-optimal performance with simple greedy policies; hierarchy addresses poor scaling; experiments demonstrate efficiency (no numbers).
cards.limitations: Greedy policies underlie the approach; no learned policy; pose/identity details not stated in abstract; effectiveness claim only qualitative.
cards.citation: Ngo Anh Vien, Marc Toussaint. Touch based POMDP manipulation via sequential submodular optimization. IEEE-RAS International Conference on Humanoid Robots (Humanoids), 2015. doi:10.1109/humanoids.2015.7363566

cards.title: TACTFUL: Tactile-Driven Exploration For Object Localization and Identification in Confined Environments
cards.problem: Vision-free tactile exploration to find, localize and identify objects in confined workspaces.
cards.method: Single policy trained entirely on real hardware without simulation, balancing global exploration and local surface refinement via a dynamic reward schedule; identification via tactile reconstruction on multi-fingered robot.
cards.findings: Achieves 77% success with 0.015 m average reconstruction error and outperforms baseline approaches on real-world objects.
cards.limitations: Identification via reconstruction rather than pose-belief inference (inferred); not an information-bound-trained policy (reward schedule); real-hardware training is data-costly (inferred); no free-space evidence stated; latency not stated in abstract.
cards.citation: Shivani Kamtikar, Chung Hee Kim, Camilla Tabasso, et al.. TACTFUL: Tactile-Driven Exploration For Object Localization and Identification in Confined Environments. arXiv (Cornell University), 2026. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2606.24712

cards.title: Reinforcement Learning Based Tactile Sensing for Active Point Cloud Acquisition, Recognition and Localization
cards.problem: Active point cloud acquisition for recognition and localization with tactile or laser sensor.
cards.method: RL agent jointly trained with classifier and pose estimator; rewards for classification, exploration and pose estimation.
cards.data: Compared with active and passive hard-coded sampling strategies; realistic and similar objects with workspace position uncertainty.
cards.findings: Framework compared against active and passive strategies with state-of-the-art classifiers; evaluated with realistic similar objects and position uncertainty (no numbers in abstract).
cards.limitations: Learned policy but rewards are task rewards, not information-gain bounds (inferred); results not quantified in abstract; latency not stated; free-space evidence not mentioned.
cards.citation: Kévin Riou, Kaiwen Dong, Kévin Subrin, et al.. Reinforcement Learning Based Tactile Sensing for Active Point Cloud Acquisition, Recognition and Localization. IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing, 2024. doi:10.1109/jstsp.2024.3431203

cards.title: Seeing By Haptic Glance: Reinforcement Learning Based 3d Object Recognition
cards.problem: Recognize 3D objects from limited haptic contacts.
cards.method: RL framework where haptic exploration (agent predicts next position) is optimized simultaneously with recognition; reward only on correct recognition.
cards.metrics: Recognition accuracy (values not stated in abstract).
cards.findings: Proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art models (no numbers).
cards.limitations: Classification only, no pose estimation (inferred); sparse terminal reward only; datasets and numbers not given in abstract; latency not stated.
cards.citation: Kévin Riou, Suiyi Ling, Guillaume Gallot, et al.. Seeing By Haptic Glance: Reinforcement Learning Based 3d Object Recognition. Proceedings - International Conference on Image Processing, 2021. doi:10.1109/icip42928.2021.9506734

cards.title: Learning When to Stop: Efficient Active Tactile Perception with Deep Reinforcement Learning
cards.problem: Learn when to stop haptic exploration to balance sample cost and misclassification cost.
cards.method: Extends Haptic Attention Model with hybrid action space (continuous glance location plus discrete decision to classify) using deep RL.
cards.data: Handcrafted dataset allowing computation of the most efficient glance locations.
cards.findings: Optimized number of glances while maintaining reasonable accuracy (no numbers in abstract).
cards.limitations: Classification only, no pose (inferred); handcrafted dataset; fixed-structure RL, not EIG-bound trained; latency not stated.
cards.citation: Christopher Niemann, David P. Leins, Luca Lach, et al.. Learning When to Stop: Efficient Active Tactile Perception with Deep Reinforcement Learning. IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), 2024. doi:10.1109/iros58592.2024.10801966

cards.title: Tactile MNIST: Benchmarking Active Tactile Perception
cards.problem: Lack of standardized benchmarks for active tactile perception.
cards.method: Tactile MNIST Benchmark Suite, Gymnasium-compatible, tasks: localization, classification, volume estimation; CycleGAN for tactile rendering.
cards.data: 13,500 synthetic 3D MNIST digit models and 153,600 real-world tactile samples collected from 600 3D printed digits.
cards.findings: Provides open-source benchmark and dataset with standardized protocols; no method results reported in abstract.
cards.limitations: Digit shapes, not general objects (inferred); no pose or identity jointly (inferred); benchmark only; no policy performance reported in abstract.
cards.citation: Tim Schneider, Duret, Guillaume, Cristiana de Farias, et al.. Tactile MNIST: Benchmarking Active Tactile Perception. arXiv (Cornell University), 2025. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2506.06361

cards.title: TANDEM3D: Active Tactile Exploration for 3D Object Recognition
cards.problem: 3D object recognition with tactile exploration.
cards.method: TANDEM3D: co-training of exploration and decision making; PointNet++ encoder on contact positions and normals; 6DOF movement.
cards.data: Trained entirely in simulation, validated in real-world experiments.
cards.metrics: Accuracy; number of actions; robustness to sensor noise.
cards.findings: Higher accuracy and fewer actions than state-of-the-art baselines and more robust to types and amounts of sensor noise (no numbers).
cards.limitations: Recognition only, no pose estimation (inferred); learned policy via task co-training, not EIG-bound; closed set of objects (inferred); latency not stated.
cards.citation: Jingxi Xu, Han X. Lin, Shuran Song, et al.. TANDEM3D: Active Tactile Exploration for 3D Object Recognition. Proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation/Proceedings, 2023. doi:10.1109/icra48891.2023.10161091

cards.title: Active Visuo-Tactile Interactive Robotic Perception for Accurate Object Pose Estimation in Dense Clutter
cards.problem: Object pose estimation in dense clutter.
cards.method: Declutter graph; translation-invariant Quaternion filter; active visual and tactile points chosen by maximizing expected information gain.
cards.data: Two robots on randomized dense cluttered scenes; ablation baselines.
cards.findings: Up to 36% improvement in pose accuracy compared to the active vision baseline.
cards.limitations: EIG maximization is per-point greedy (inferred); needs two robots and vision; no learned touch policy; identity not estimated jointly; latency not stated.
cards.citation: Prajval Kumar Murali, Anirvan Dutta, Michael Gentner, et al.. Active Visuo-Tactile Interactive Robotic Perception for Accurate Object Pose Estimation in Dense Clutter. IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, 2022. doi:10.1109/lra.2022.3150045

cards.title: Shared visuo-tactile interactive perception for robust object pose estimation
cards.problem: Robust pose estimation of novel objects in dense clutter through shared visuo-tactile perception.
cards.method: Stochastic Translation-Invariant Quaternion Filter; hand-eye calibration; joint information gain criterion for active representation.
cards.data: Standard datasets for pose estimation and real-robot experiments with opaque, transparent and specular objects in randomised clutter.
cards.findings: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods in pose estimation accuracy for dense visual and sparse tactile point clouds (no numbers).
cards.limitations: Requires two-robot setup and vision (inferred); information-gain selection appears greedy (inferred); no learned amortized policy; latency not stated.
cards.citation: Prajval Kumar Murali, Bernd Porr, Mohsen Kaboli. Shared visuo-tactile interactive perception for robust object pose estimation. The International Journal of Robotics Research, 2024. doi:10.1177/02783649241301443

cards.title: Active Tactile Exploration Based on Cost-Aware Information Gain Maximization
cards.problem: Object shape reconstruction from sparse tactile data.
cards.method: Information Gain Estimation Function combining information gain and expected cost to pick next best touch target.
cards.data: Simulation using 48 publicly available object models compared with Gaussian process based exploration.
cards.findings: Shows performance in exploration efficiency, cost-awareness and suitability for real tactile sensing (no numbers).
cards.limitations: Shape reconstruction, not pose or identity; greedy next-best-touch (inferred); validated in simulation; latency not stated.
cards.citation: Simon Ottenhaus, Lukas Kaul, Nikolaus Vahrenkamp, et al.. Active Tactile Exploration Based on Cost-Aware Information Gain Maximization. International Journal of Humanoid Robotics, 2018. doi:10.1142/s0219843618500159

cards.title: AcTExplore: Active Tactile Exploration of Unknown Objects
cards.problem: Efficient tactile exploration of unknown objects.
cards.method: RL-driven active tactile exploration that incrementally collects tactile data and reconstructs 3D shapes.
cards.data: Trained on primitive shapes, tested on unseen YCB objects.
cards.findings: Average of 95.97% IoU coverage on unseen YCB objects while just being trained on primitive shapes.
cards.limitations: Reconstruction, not pose/identity estimation; coverage reward rather than information bound (inferred); latency not stated.
cards.citation: Amir-Hossein Shahidzadeh, Seong Jong Yoo, Pavan Mantripragada, et al.. AcTExplore: Active Tactile Exploration of Unknown Objects. arXiv (Cornell University), 2023. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2310.08745

cards.title: Learning efficient haptic shape exploration with a rigid tactile sensor array
cards.problem: Learn haptic exploration for object identification.
cards.method: Haptic Attention Model: recurrent attention inspired RL with feature extractor and RNN; reward on success only.
cards.data: Simulated 3D environment with rigid static objects (edge, flat, convex), 16 × 16 tactile sensor array; tested with four different objects.
cards.findings: Achieved results close to 100% while performing object contour exploration.
cards.limitations: Simulation, four objects, simple features; no pose estimation (inferred); sparse success-only reward; latency not stated.
cards.citation: Sascha Fleer, Alexandra Moringen, Roberta L. Klatzky, et al.. Learning efficient haptic shape exploration with a rigid tactile sensor array. PLoS ONE, 2020. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0226880

cards.title: TactoFind: A Tactile Only System for Object Retrieval
cards.problem: Tactile-only retrieval of free objects without vision.
cards.method: System with sparse fingertip touch on dexterous hand to localize, identify and grasp novel objects.
cards.data: Real dexterous hand (details not stated in abstract).
cards.findings: Presents a system that localizes, identifies and grasps novel objects without visual feedback (no numbers).
cards.limitations: Quantitative results absent from abstract; exploration policy details not stated; latency not stated.
cards.citation: Sameer Pai, Tao Chen, Megha H. Tippur, et al.. TactoFind: A Tactile Only System for Object Retrieval. Proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation/Proceedings, 2023. doi:10.1109/icra48891.2023.10160289

cards.title: MultiSCOPE: Disambiguating In-Hand Object Poses with Proprioception and Tactile Feedback
cards.problem: In-hand object pose disambiguation using proprioception and tactile feedback.
cards.method: Tool segmentation routine, consistency loss across interactions, loss explaining external force-torque; bimanual frictional contacts.
cards.findings: Significant improvement in object pose estimation over single interactions (no numbers).
cards.limitations: In-hand setting with grasped objects; contact interactions not chosen by information-gain policy (inferred); latency not stated.
cards.citation: Andrea Sipos, Nima Fazeli. MultiSCOPE: Disambiguating In-Hand Object Poses with Proprioception and Tactile Feedback. Robotics: Science and Systems, 2023. doi:10.15607/rss.2023.xix.078

cards.title: Belief-Driven Tactile Exploration for Vision-Free Plug–Socket Insertion
cards.problem: Vision-free plug-socket insertion by estimating socket pose from contact.
cards.method: Particle belief over planar position and orientation updated via contact height measurements from a CAD-based collision model; contact-guided tangential motions; Halton-based exploration trajectory; anisotropic impedance controller.
cards.data: Several connector types: power sockets, USB, Ethernet.
cards.findings: Demonstrates robust pose convergence and reliable insertion under substantial initial pose uncertainty without visual feedback (no numbers).
cards.limitations: Planar pose only; exploration is heuristic/low-discrepancy coverage, not information-optimized policy (inferred); known CAD model; no identity inference; latency not stated.
cards.citation: Boris Kuster, Aleš Ude, Bojan Nemec. Belief-Driven Tactile Exploration for Vision-Free Plug–Socket Insertion. IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, 2026. doi:10.1109/lra.2026.3739596

cards.title: Manipulation in the Blind: Motion Planning for Manipulation under Uncertainty using Contacts
cards.problem: Contact-based planning for manipulation under pose and environmental uncertainty.
cards.method: Search-based POMDP planning: experience-based policy database, hierarchical online planning, lazy belief-update heuristic search; torque-based contact detection with learned occupancy estimators.
cards.data: Simulation and a real UR10e manipulator on two domestic tasks (valve under sink, shelf retrieval).
cards.findings: Lazy solvers substantially reduce planning time while preserving solution quality; framework evaluated on valve and shelf tasks (no numbers).
cards.limitations: Thesis; POMDP planning is computationally expensive (stated); task-specific, not identity inference; amortization limited to a database of previously solved similar POMDPs.
cards.citation: Muhammad Suhail Saleem. Manipulation in the Blind: Motion Planning for Manipulation under Uncertainty using Contacts. KiltHub Repository, 2026. doi:10.1184/r1/32622771

cards.title: Pose estimation for planar contact manipulation with manifold particle filters
cards.problem: Pose estimation of a pushed object using contact sensors.
cards.method: Manifold particle filter sampling from dual proposal on the contact manifold; three sampling techniques.
cards.data: Simulation and real robot with commercially available tactile sensors.
cards.findings: All three techniques outperform the conventional particle filter in both speed and accuracy in simulation; real robot tracks pushed object pose.
cards.limitations: Estimation only, no action selection; planar pushing; contact and no-contact discrimination exploited as manifold structure but not for touch choice (inferred).
cards.citation: Michael C. Koval, Nancy S. Pollard, Siddhartha S Srinivasa. Pose estimation for planar contact manipulation with manifold particle filters. The International Journal of Robotics Research, 2015. doi:10.1177/0278364915571007

cards.title: Contact-based in-hand pose estimation using Bayesian state estimation and particle filtering
cards.problem: High-precision in-hand pose estimation with force sensor only.
cards.method: Bayesian state estimation with particle filtering from contact.
cards.findings: Determines object position to a precision of under 1 mm without part-specific jigs; sub-millimeter precision.
cards.limitations: In-hand position estimation; touches not selected by information policy (inferred); needs known rigid object; latency not stated.
cards.citation: Felix von Drigalski, Shohei Taniguchi, Robert Lee, et al.. Contact-based in-hand pose estimation using Bayesian state estimation and particle filtering. Proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation/Proceedings, 2020. doi:10.1109/icra40945.2020.9196640

cards.title: Localizing external contact using proprioceptive sensors: The Contact Particle Filter
cards.problem: Localize external contacts on rigid body robots without external sensing.
cards.method: Contact Particle Filter finds contact points best explaining joint torque.
cards.findings: Tracks multiple external contacts and compares favorably with existing approaches (no numbers).
cards.limitations: Contact localization on the robot, not object pose; simulation only (inferred).
cards.citation: Lucas Manuelli, Russ Tedrake. Localizing external contact using proprioceptive sensors: The Contact Particle Filter. IEEE/RJS International Conference on Intelligent RObots and Systems, 2016. doi:10.1109/IROS.2016.7759743

cards.title: Tac2Pose: Tactile object pose estimation from the first touch
cards.problem: Tactile pose estimation from the first touch for known objects.
cards.method: Simulate contact shapes for dense pose set; contrastive object-specific embedding; outputs pose distribution; calibration from RGB tactile to binary contact shapes.
cards.data: Quantitative results for 20 objects; scanned models also tested.
cards.findings: High accuracy from distinctive tactile observations; produces pose distributions; improves on priors; accuracy with scanned models comparable to CAD (qualitative).
cards.limitations: Object-specific model per known object; known object set; single-touch, no touch selection; latency not stated.
cards.citation: Maria Bauzá, Antonia Bronars, Alberto Rodríguez. Tac2Pose: Tactile object pose estimation from the first touch. The International Journal of Robotics Research, 2023. doi:10.1177/02783649231196925

cards.title: Learning Bayes Filter Models for Tactile Localization
cards.problem: Tactile localization of grippers with imprecise kinematics.
cards.method: Learnable Bayes filter with observation model conditioned on visual maps plus motion model, trained self-supervised in simulation.
cards.data: Tabletop task in simulation and on real robot.
cards.findings: Generalizes over different sizes, shapes and configurations of objects in simulation and real robot (no numbers).
cards.limitations: Localizes gripper not object; needs visual maps; no action selection stated.
cards.citation: Tarik Keleştemur, Colin Keil, John Peter Whitney, et al.. Learning Bayes Filter Models for Tactile Localization. IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), 2020. doi:10.1109/iros45743.2020.9341420

cards.title: TacLoc: Global Tactile Localization on Objects from a Registration Perspective
cards.problem: Global tactile localization of objects.
cards.method: One-shot point cloud registration; graph-theoretic partial-to-full registration with normal-guided graph pruning and hypothesis-and-verification.
cards.data: YCB dataset and real-world objects with two visual-tactile sensors.
cards.findings: Improved performance without rendered data or pre-trained models (no numbers).
cards.limitations: One-shot, no touch selection; known object models (inferred); numbers not in abstract.
cards.citation: Zhang, Zirui, Boyang Zhang, Fumin Zhang, et al.. TacLoc: Global Tactile Localization on Objects from a Registration Perspective. arXiv (Cornell University), 2026. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2603.10565

cards.title: You Only Touch Once: 6-DoF Object Pose Estimation from Single Tactile Contact
cards.problem: 6-DoF pose from a single pair of simultaneous contacts.
cards.method: Coarse-to-fine contact localization network pretrained on virtual patches, closed-form normal-aware SVD solver.
cards.data: Four geometrically diverse objects; real GelSight dataset.
cards.findings: Accurate contact localization and pose estimation, outperforming vision-based and geometric baselines especially when vision is unreliable.
cards.limitations: Four objects; requires two simultaneous contacts; known models; no active selection.
cards.citation: Pengfei Ye, Yuxiang Ma, Haonan Chen, et al.. You Only Touch Once: 6-DoF Object Pose Estimation from Single Tactile Contact. arXiv (Cornell University), 2026. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2606.28899

cards.title: In-Hand Object Pose Tracking via Contact Feedback and GPU-Accelerated Robotic Simulation
cards.problem: Track in-hand object pose during manipulation.
cards.method: GPU-accelerated parallel simulation with derivative-free sample-based optimizers.
cards.metrics: Point cloud distance error; update rate.
cards.findings: Runs in real-time (30Hz) on a single GPU; average point cloud distance error of 6mm in simulation and 13mm in real-world.
cards.limitations: Requires GPU simulation; tracking not action selection.
cards.citation: Jacky Liang, Ankur Handa, Karl Van Wyk, et al.. In-Hand Object Pose Tracking via Contact Feedback and GPU-Accelerated Robotic Simulation. Proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation/Proceedings, 2020. doi:10.1109/icra40945.2020.9197117

cards.title: Learning a State Estimator for Tactile In-Hand Manipulation
cards.problem: Pose estimation with proprioceptive feedback only.
cards.method: Differentiable particle filter with learned proposal and SE(3) Lie-group update.
cards.data: Simulation, domain randomization, real DLR-Hand II.
cards.findings: Estimator runs online with update rates of more than 100 Hz on a single CPU core.
cards.limitations: Passive state estimation; qualitative real experiments.
cards.citation: Lennart Röstel, Leon Sievers, Johannes Pitz, et al.. Learning a State Estimator for Tactile In-Hand Manipulation. IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), 2022. doi:10.1109/iros47612.2022.9981730

cards.title: Learning Tactile Models for Factor Graph-based Estimation
cards.problem: Object pose tracking from touch during planar pushing.
cards.method: Learned tactile observation models in factor graph.
cards.data: ~150 real-world planar pushing sequences, three object shapes.
cards.findings: Reliable object tracking using only tactile feedback for ~150 real sequences across three object shapes.
cards.limitations: Planar pushing, three shapes; passive tracking.
cards.citation: Paloma Sodhi, M. Kaess, Mustafa Mukadam, et al.. Learning Tactile Models for Factor Graph-based Estimation. IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation, 2021. doi:10.1109/ICRA48506.2021.9561011

cards.title: Tactile SLAM: Real-time inference of shape and pose from planar pushing
cards.problem: Real-time shape and pose from planar pushing.
cards.method: Online SLAM with GPIS regression and factor graph pose estimation.
cards.findings: Infers shape and pose in real-time (no numbers).
cards.limitations: Planar pushing; no touch selection; unknown-object shape instead of identity.
cards.citation: Sudharshan Suresh, Maria Bauzá, Kuan‐Ting Yu, et al.. Tactile SLAM: Real-time inference of shape and pose from planar pushing. Proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation/Proceedings, 2021. doi:10.1109/icra48506.2021.9562060

cards.title: NeuralFeels with neural fields: Visuotactile perception for in-hand manipulation
cards.problem: Visuotactile pose and shape in in-hand manipulation.
cards.method: Neural field plus pose graph.
cards.findings: Final reconstruction F scores of 81% and average pose drifts of 4.7 millimeters, reduced to 2.3 millimeters with known models; up to 94% tracking improvement under occlusion.
cards.limitations: Needs vision and multifingered hand; policy proprioception-driven, not information-driven.
cards.citation: Sudharshan Suresh, Haozhi Qi, Tingfan Wu, et al.. NeuralFeels with neural fields: Visuotactile perception for in-hand manipulation. Science Robotics, 2024. doi:10.1126/scirobotics.adl0628

cards.title: Multifidelity Sampling for Fast Bayesian Shape Estimation With Tactile Exploration
cards.problem: Fast Bayesian shape estimation from few touches.
cards.method: Next sample chosen by mutual information and local curvature.
cards.findings: Reconstructs recognizable three dimensional shapes using only around optimally selected 0.4% of the original dataset (less than 1%).
cards.limitations: Greedy one-step selection (inferred); shape only.
cards.citation: Shiyi Yang, Soo Jung Jeon, Jongeun Choi. Multifidelity Sampling for Fast Bayesian Shape Estimation With Tactile Exploration. IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics, 2019. doi:10.1109/tii.2019.2948853

cards.title: Object shape estimation and modeling, based on sparse Gaussian process implicit surfaces, combining visual data and tactile exploration
cards.problem: Shape estimation with sparse GPIS from vision and touch.
cards.method: Sparse GPIS.
cards.data: Synthetic and real data from two robots.
cards.findings: Sparse GPs approximate full GP reliably, enable distinguishing objects and efficient exploration.
cards.limitations: Shape modeling; action planning is future enabled.
cards.citation: Gabriela Zarzar Gandler, Carl Henrik Ek, Mårten Björkman, et al.. Object shape estimation and modeling, based on sparse Gaussian process implicit surfaces, combining visual data and tactile exploration. Robotics and Autonomous Systems, 2020. doi:10.1016/j.robot.2020.103433

cards.title: Deep Adaptive Design: Amortizing Sequential Bayesian Experimental Design
cards.problem: Amortize sequential BED.
cards.method: DAD design network, contrastive bounds.
